summary: The classification, converse, shear invariance, fiber normalization, and intrinsic residual-rank formula are all proved without gaps. The concavity and convexity of attained fiber extrema force exact affine interpolation on every closed orthant simplex, including singleton boundary fibers; opposite axis midpoints give precisely the necessary entrywise bounds, and those bounds make every lower endpoint convex and every upper endpoint concave. The affine shear preserves each integer fiber's d-dimensional volume and bijects containing closed halfspaces. The positive support and actual centroid normalization match the supplied predecessor conventions, and the rank identity is applicable after full dimension is established. Small cases n=d=1, R at or below 1, R just above 1, zero B, and saturated coefficients provide no counterexample.
